endorsements.quote: To rigorously assess both bene fits and risks, AI applications in medicine must be evaluated in well-designed prospective studies using patient-relevant endpoints, such as reduced disease-related mortality, improved diseasefree survival, or gains in quality-adjusted life years.
Equally important are robust transparency requirements that ensure clear documentation of data sources, population characteristics, model development processes, and known limitations.

Key strategies will include the use of large, diverse, and representative datasets, the application of statistical debiasing and fairness-aware modeling techniques, and Caspers and Heinrichs European Radiology Page 3 of 6 rigorous model evaluation, ideally through prospective and multicenter clinical trials.
Consequently, it will be essential to employ strategies that tightly control such systems and strictly delimit the environments in which they operate in healthcare settings.

unlisted_practices: Establish robust quality assurance frameworks enabling post-deployment surveillance, continuous performance monitoring, and ongoing benefit-risk assessment of AI.
Advance research on human-AI interaction in medicine and develop strategies to mitigate automation bias.
Integrate automation bias mitigation strategies into medical education and physician training.
Reform medical curricula to include digital literacy, data science and AI fundamentals, ethical and legal considerations, and human-AI interaction training.
Give patients the opportunity to understand AI, question its application, and, where appropriate, refuse its use.
Manage patient and public expectations of medical AI and educate patients while keeping the doctor-patient relationship central.
Incorporate patient perspectives in the design and implementation of AI tools in healthcare.
Evaluate AI for effects on clinical workflows, resource utilization, and health-economic outcomes.
